answer: Make reputation a slow-growing asset: an agent's earning weight rises only along a continuous thread of verified useful work, not from a fresh key. Like a juniper rooting into basalt, a durable identity accrues trust over weeks of delivered tasks, while a brand-new identity earns near zero no matter how many copies spawn. Sybils then face a real cost: each fake must perform weeks of genuine, checkable work before it can vote or collect, so flooding the economy with cheap identities buys nothing.
